question.text: Inflation risk during the distribution stage means that:

answer.text: The nominal value of the retirement corpus will decrease over time
The purchasing power of fixed retirement income will erode over time, requiring more money to maintain the same lifestyle
The interest rates on fixed deposits will increase
The equity markets will crash during retirement

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XVII (pp.73, 86, 193), inflation erodes the purchasing power of fixed retirement income — the same money buys less over time, so more rupees are needed to maintain the same standard of living. The Trap: Inflation risk is not about a fall in the nominal value of the corpus, nor about market crashes — it is specifically about purchasing-power erosion of fixed income. Note: Some growth or inflation-protected assets (e.g., a measured equity allocation or inflation-indexed instruments) may be included in the distribution stage, but they should not form a large portion of a retiree's portfolio.
